name: recv-table
bug: promiscuous learning: drops the target test of RFC 826 line 214, so any packet clearing the hardware/protocol gate installs an entry for its sender pair even when the packet was not addressed to this node (the ARP cache-poisoning enabler)

name: merge-before-opcode
bug: opcode validation hoisted above the merge: an opcode that is neither REQUEST nor REPLY is discarded without touching the table, contradicting lines 227-229 ('merged into the table before the opcode is looked at')

name: reply-emit
bug: the literal-swap misreading of lines 221-222: the reply exchanges sender and target fields without substituting the local addresses, so it advertises the requester's own binding back at it and reads ar$tha, which line 312 says has no meaning in a request

name: resolve-out
bug: a generated REQUEST carries the address being resolved in ar$spa instead of this node's own protocol address, breaking the local form of the no-propagation claim at lines 459-466 (Stage B gap G-2)

name: supersede-two
bug: first-writer-wins: the second reception adds a binding but refuses to overwrite an existing one, the common anti-spoofing bolt-on, contradicting lines 231-234 ('the new hardware address supersedes the old one')

name: learn-sender-only
bug: learning both ends: the target pair <ar$pro, ar$tpa> -> ar$tha is cached alongside the sender triplet, entering a binding the sender was never asked to fill in (line 312) and that no clause in lines 209-218 authorises
